statement: Six equal squares make a rectangle 3 squares long and 2 squares wide. The distance all the way round the rectangle is 30 cm. How long is the side of one square?

choices.misconception: I shared the 30 cm between the 6 squares, but the distance round is made of the small sides on the outline, not of squares.
I shared 30 cm into 3 + 2 = 5 parts, using only one long side and one short side.
I shared 30 cm between the 3 squares in one row.
I halved 30 cm and stopped there.

hints: Draw the rectangle and count the small square sides around the outside.
The distance round is made of many equal small square sides. Count how many of them go all the way round the rectangle, then share the 30 cm equally between them.
Along the top there are 3 small sides, down the right 2, along the bottom 3 and up the left 2. Share 30 cm between all of them.

solutions.reliable: Going round the rectangle you pass 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 = 10 sides of small squares. Those 10 equal sides make 30 cm, so each side is 3 cm. Check: the rectangle is 9 cm by 6 cm, and 9 + 6 + 9 + 6 = 30. The idea to keep: count how many equal pieces make up the outline, then share.
solutions.elegant: Try each choice. If a side is 3 cm, the rectangle is 9 cm long and 6 cm wide, and 9 + 6 + 9 + 6 = 30 cm. That matches, so the answer is 3 cm. The idea to keep: when working backwards is hard, test the answer choices.

whyOnTest: Working backwards from a perimeter tests counting the equal edges on the outline, not the squares.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
